tools.notes: [sweep 2026-09-11] Page alive, claims supported. access paid -> freemium: reachable via the free Gemini app with a limited daily quota (third-party guides; DeepMind page lists Gemini-app availability without pricing). Note Nano Banana 2 / 2 Lite now exist; Pro remains the current high-fidelity model page.

tools.name: OpenAI Prism
tools.description: Free AI-native LaTeX workspace on GPT-5.2: whole-document writing and proofreading assistance, reference management, image-to-LaTeX for photographed equations and whiteboard sketches, agentic literature search with citation suggestions, and real-time collaboration with unlimited collaborators.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: A full AI-first LaTeX editor free with any ChatGPT account — the whole-document AI context (not per-sentence) plus built-in arXiv literature agent Adoption: HKUST Library news page recommending it to academic writers (fetched); Engadget and The Decoder launch coverage seen in search; app live at prism.openai.com (fetched, sign-in shell) Built on acquired Crixet platform. Cloud-only; HKUST cautions on uploading unpublished/sensitive work and possible future paywalling of advanced features. openai.com/prism blocks bot fetching (403).

tools.name: Overleaf AI Assist
tools.description: AI built into the standard collaborative LaTeX editor: explains and fixes LaTeX compile errors, generates tables and equations from images or prompts (TeXGPT), and gives Writefull-powered language feedback trained on published papers. Free daily allowances on all plans.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: LaTeX error diagnosis and repair inside the editor 20M+ researchers already write in — no copy-pasting code into a chatbot Adoption: Official overleaf.com/about/ai-features page (fetched); docs.overleaf.com AI-features pages; Overleaf blog 'Overleaf AI now a part of Overleaf plans' (July 2026); Overleaf itself appears across university libguides (e.g. Bristol) Since July 2026 included in all plans with daily caps (quota resets ~72h); paid plans raise allowances. Error assist uses OpenAI as third party.

tools.name: Papers AI
tools.provider: Digital Science (built by the Overleaf team)
tools.description: Offline-first AI research workspace: write in LaTeX, Typst, Markdown or Word alongside Jupyter notebooks and CSVs, with a context-aware assistant that reads drafts, data and references together. Compiles locally in-browser; can run entirely on local models via Ollama/LM Studio/vLLM.
tools.notes:
[discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: AI-assisted scholarly writing that never sends data to the cloud (local models, local compile) — the GDPR/sensitive-data option; also the only AI-assisted Typst workflow found Adoption: Digital Science press release, launch 4 Aug 2026 (fetched); product page live with free tier (fetched); too new for libguides Two weeks old at review time — no independent adoption evidence yet. Distinct from ReadCube Papers despite the name. Paid-tier pricing not published on fetched pages.
[sweep 2026-09-11] Alive; paid tier now published: Plus GBP 10/month (5x AI allowance) alongside Free — supersedes the 'pricing not published' note. Description still accurate.

tools.name: Trinka
tools.description: Upload a .tex file and get it proofread with LaTeX commands untouched: returns a corrected LaTeX file plus a Word file with tracked changes, a language-quality score, and revision breakdown. Style-guide aware (APA, AMA, IEEE).
tools.notes:
[discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Batch proofreading of a whole .tex manuscript outside any editor, with tracked-changes Word output co-authors can review — bridges LaTeX and Word-based collaborators Adoption: Official Trinka feature and news pages (fetched); G2 review presence seen in search; no libguide sighting confirmed Credit-based: 1 credit per 5,000 words, 4 free credits/month on Basic. Parent Enago also behind catalog's 'Enago AI Disclosure' — different product. Broader Trinka overlaps Paperpal; propose only the LaTeX proofreader angle.
[sweep 2026-09-11] Domain blocked for fetch; page confirmed live via search (exact URL and title), credit model unchanged.

tools.name: Writefull
tools.description: Language feedback for scientific text from models trained on millions of published journal articles, delivered inside Overleaf (edits in LaTeX source), Word, or a standalone Revise uploader. Adds paraphrasing, abstract/title generation, and TeXGPT table/equation code generation.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Sentence-level feedback calibrated to published-paper conventions rather than general English; corrections applied directly within LaTeX source code Adoption: Multiple university libguides fetched via search: Montclair State, CSIR (South Africa), Nazarbayev University; integrated natively into Overleaf Premium ~$150/yr (June 2026 listing). Writefull Cite (flags sentences needing a citation) is institution-license only. States texts are not stored or used for training.

tools.name: Enago AI Disclosure
tools.description: Generate an AI Disclosure Statement for your manuscript that you can use while submitting your manuscript to a publisher.
tools.notes: [sweep 2026-08-18] Listed URL is Enago homepage; dedicated generator page fetched and confirmed (form, statement delivered as PDF via email). No payment step shown; 'free' not explicitly stated on page.

tools.name: Manusights
tools.description: Pre-submission manuscript diagnostic: free Readiness Scan in minutes plus a $39 Full Review in about 30 minutes. Verifies citations claim-by-claim against live databases with a retraction gate and analyses figures. Anthropic privacy partner; manuscripts not used for model training.
tools.notes:
[sweep 2026-08-18] description flagged: Homepage fetched: free Readiness Scan + paid Full Review now $39 (description says $29) + human Expert tier. Citation verification, figure analysis, Anthropic privacy/no-training claims confirmed; signup open.
[sweep 2026-09-11] Description corrected: paid report is $39 (was $29, flagged already in Aug); 'zero-retention' replaced with the page's own 'bounded retention / not used for training' wording.

tools.name: Proofig + PubShield
tools.description: Image integrity AI (Proofig) paired with iThenticate text-similarity screening via PubShield. Brings figure-duplication detection and plagiarism checks into a single pre-publication workflow used by publishers and institutions.

tools.name: Prophy
tools.description: Semantic reviewer-matching platform used by publishers and funding agencies to find conflict-free referees for a manuscript or proposal, ranked across 101M+ researcher profiles and 196M+ papers; integrates with Editorial Manager. Demo-request access, no public pricing.
tools.notes:
[sweep 2026-08-18] prophy.science 301s to prophy.ai, which bot-blocks fetchers (403). blog.prophy.ai and search confirm Referee Finder for publishers/funders, ~96M profiles, Editorial Manager integration. Pricing/access not visible anywhere fetched.
[sweep 2026-09-11] Alive, URL/provider correct, numbers now 101M+ profiles / 196M+ papers. Open question for Michaela: site offers only 'Request a demo' (B2B for publishers/funders), so gate 2 (usable this week) looks failed for a student — decide whether it stays active/core as the editor-side exemplar with access left 'unknown', or moves to candidate. Not resolvable by fetching.

tools.name: QED Science
tools.description: Critical Thinking AI that breaks a manuscript or grant into its constituent claims, flags logical and methodological gaps, and ranks novelty against studies in the field (QED Score). Free for academic researchers; enterprise tier for pharma/biotech. In use at 1,500 institutions in 70+ countries.
tools.notes: [sweep 2026-09-11] '1,000+ institutions' -> '1,500 institutions / 70+ countries' per QED Science press release 2026-06-24 (own blog). Site now brands the product 'QED Science' / 'QED Score'; 'q.e.d.' no longer visible - consider renaming entry. access freemium confirmed.

tools.name: RefereeBio
tools.provider: RefereeBio (no legal entity named on site)
tools.description: Simulates pre-submission peer review of life-science manuscripts: three reviewer critiques, statistical-methods audit, journal-fit ranking across 150+ journals. Revision-check compares a revised manuscript against reviewer comments and drafts point-by-point rebuttals.
tools.notes:
[grok-gap-hunt 2026-08-18, independently verified] All section-10 claims confirmed on homepage (free Starter month: 3 reviews/3 revision checks/3 edits, no card; AI-provider clause). No legal entity or team named; keep candidate.
[sweep 2026-09-11] Still no legal entity, founders, address or jurisdiction on /about, /legal or /security; self-described 'early access'. Fails gate 4 (recommendable to students). Keep candidate.

tools.name: RegCheck
tools.provider: Psychology of Digitalisation group, University of Bern (SNSF-funded)
tools.description: Upload a preregistration (or ClinicalTrials.gov link) plus the final paper; an LLM compares them dimension-by-dimension and flags deviations, quoting verbatim text from both documents so every judgement is checkable. Free, with API.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Preregistration-vs-paper consistency checking — automating a review step editors demonstrably skip; nothing else in or near the catalog does this Adoption: arXiv paper 2601.13330 (Cummins et al.); featured as a module in the scienceverse Metacheck manual Some modules marked coming soon. Full texts are sent to the RegCheck server — consider before uploading unpublished manuscripts.

tools.name: Review-it
tools.description: Uploads a manuscript, thesis or proposal (PDF/DOCX) and returns an AI peer review with strengths, weaknesses and suggested fixes, plus a pre-submission checklist (scope, citations, desk-rejection risk), journal finder and a reference checker for fake or broken citations. Per-document from $6.99; unlimited $59/month.
tools.notes: [sweep 2026-09-11] Alive (rendered in browser; plain fetch returns empty SPA shell). Description rewritten capability-first with verified pricing; removed the 50%-of-researchers Nature statistic, which is not about the product. Small vendor with no independent coverage found — gate 4 evidence is thin but pricing/privacy statements are on the page.

tools.name: Reviewer3
tools.description: AI peer review platform: integrity checks (hallucinated or retracted citations, AI-generated text), claim-by-claim evidence decomposition, and panel review of study design, data and scope, with modes for author self-review, reviewer support and editorial triage. Claims 98.5% accuracy separating real from fabricated citations.
tools.notes: [sweep 2026-09-11] Positioning changed on homepage (integrity/claim verification focus; EQUATOR/journal-specific wording gone) — description rewritten. Pricing page unreadable; third-party reports a free first review + $19/review + $29/mo, which would make access freemium — confirm on site before changing.

tools.name: SciScore
tools.description: Paste a methods section, get a 1-10 rigor score auditing blinding, randomization, power analysis, and resource identifiability (antibodies, cell lines, RRIDs) against NIH/ARRIVE guidelines. Ten free reports yearly via ORCID sign-in.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Automated rigor-and-reporting audit of your own methods section before submission — no other tool scores RRID identifiability and NIH rigor criteria Adoption: Integrated into FASEB journal submission workflow (Newswise/FASEB announcements); basis of the published Rigor and Transparency Index (iScience 2020, PMC7644557) Anita Bandrowski (RRID initiative) is CEO — credible lineage. Score reflects reporting completeness, not actual experimental quality.

tools.name: Stanford Agentic Reviewer
tools.description: Free AI peer review system by Andrew Ng's team providing rapid, actionable feedback. Grounds reviews in latest arXiv research; correlation with human reviewers (0.42) matches inter-human agreement (0.41).

tools.name: Argos
tools.description: Screens a reference list for retracted and high-risk articles before submission and sends alerts when papers in your citation network are retracted; computes daily risk scores from author histories and retraction cascades across 50M+ articles.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: retraction-risk screening of references plus proactive retraction-cascade alerts Adoption: Oncotarget lists Argos on its scientific-integrity process page; Duke Medical Center Library blog covers it among retraction-identification tools Free account 'for the entire scientific community'; institutional tier priced on request. Public benefit corporation. 2025 statistics on site.

tools.name: Imagetwin
tools.description: Scans figures (western blots, microscopy, photos) for duplications, manipulations, and AI-generated images; matches against a 150M+ published-figure database to catch cross-paper reuse. Pay-per-scan from EUR 29 makes lab-level pre-submission screening feasible.
tools.notes:
[discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Cross-paper figure matching against 150M+ published figures, purchasable as a EUR 29 one-off scan — no publisher subscription needed (Proofig's catalog entry is manuscript-level screening) Adoption: Mass General Brigham Research Computing licenses it for its researchers (rc.partners.org page, fetched), including honest guidance on limitations MGB flags a notable false-negative rate; scatterplots/FACS not covered. Differentiation vs Proofig taken from vendor pages, not independently benchmarked.
[sweep 2026-09-11] Verified; provider corrected to legal name ImageTwin AI GmbH as shown on pricing page. EUR 29 single scan and 150M+ figures still supported.

tools.name: Pangram
tools.description: Classifies text as human- or AI-written with per-document and per-sentence results via web dashboard and API; 20 free checks daily. Reports a 1-in-10,000 false-positive rate, with an independent University of Chicago evaluation.
tools.notes:
[discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: AI-text detection with the only independently evaluated sub-0.5% false-positive rate — usable for editorial screening where accusation stakes are high Adoption: arXiv technical report 2402.14873; a 2025 University of Chicago evaluation (seen via search + vendor third-party-evals page) found it the only detector meeting an FPR<=0.005 policy cap All AI-text detection is probabilistic — never sole evidence against an author. Headline accuracy figures are vendor-reported; one independent academic eval, which I saw summarized, not in full.
[sweep 2026-09-11] Provider corrected to 'Pangram Labs' as named on site; all description numbers still supported.

tools.name: Problematic Paper Screener
tools.provider: Guillaume Cabanac, IRIT / Universite de Toulouse (with Labbe & Magazinov)
tools.description: Browsable dashboard screening the literature with detectors for tortured phrases, SCIgen/Mathgen text, citejacking, Seek & Blastn nucleotide errors, problematic cell lines, and retracted or concerning references. Check a DOI before citing it, or trawl your field for flagged papers.
tools.notes:
[discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: The only public tool for checking whether a specific published paper is flagged for tortured phrases, mass-produced text, or reliance on retracted work — post-publication integrity screening for readers, not publishers Adoption: Peer-reviewed description (arXiv 2210.04895); coverage in The Conversation, Science, TechXplore; coverage credits it with contributing to 1000+ retractions Landing URL redirects to an Oracle APEX app (dbrech.irit.fr/pls/apex/f?p=9999) — data verified fresh, last update 2026-08-13. Academic side project, not a company.
[sweep 2026-09-11] Landing redirect chain still works; APEX app alive, data last updated 2026-08-13. '130M+ papers' figure not shown on the page — dropped per anti-fabrication rule; added Seek & Blastn detector.

tools.name: RefCheckAI
tools.provider: Sydney Informatics Hub, University of Sydney
tools.description: Checks whether each citation statement is actually supported by the cited source, classifying claims as supported, partially supported, not supported, or uncertain, with evidence snippets. Fine-tuned open Llama 3.1 model; free for non-commercial use.
tools.notes:
[discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Semantic citation verification — whether the cited paper supports the claim, not merely whether the reference exists (scite shows citation context but does not classify your own manuscript's claims) Adoption: University-built (Sydney Informatics Hub, NCI/NVIDIA-supported CodeFest); model weights and training data published for download Early access — web app via registration/email only. Classification accuracy not independently benchmarked. CC BY-NC 4.0.
[sweep 2026-09-11] Alive, unchanged. Still early-access via registration/email only, so fails gate 2 (usable this week). Keep candidate; page brands it 'AI Reference Checker'.

tools.name: statcheck
tools.description: Upload a PDF, DOCX, or HTML manuscript; it recomputes every APA-style statistical result (t, F, r, chi-square, Z, Q) and flags p-values inconsistent with the reported test statistic and degrees of freedom.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: recomputation-based consistency check of reported statistics — a spellchecker for stats Adoption: Used in the review workflow of Psychological Science and Journal of Experimental Social Psychology; R package on CRAN; own Wikipedia entry Rule-based automation, not an LLM — flag if catalog is strictly 'AI'. Requires APA-formatted stats; misses tables. v1.5.0 (2024). Files not stored.

tools.name: B!SON
tools.description: Paste a manuscript's title, abstract, and references; machine-learning similarity against DOAJ article and citation data ranks quality-assured open-access journals publishing similar work, with transparent per-journal reasoning and an open API.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: manuscript-driven open-access journal selection (no journal-selection tool in catalog) Adoption: SLUB Dresden library service page; DOAJ blog feature dated 2026-07-08 confirming monthly data updates; institutions can host custom instances Open source, German library-run, privacy-friendly — strong EU/GDPR fit. Landing page is a JS app; capability details verified via DOAJ/TIB pages.

tools.name: ChatSlide
tools.description: Upload a paper or paste an abstract; generates a single-page academic poster (A0 or 36x48 in) with sectioned layout, charts rendered from your data, and PubMed/Scholar citation lookup. Exports print-locked PDF or editable pptx.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: No-code hosted paper-to-poster with print-size and editable-pptx export (the accessible counterpart to Paper2Poster) Adoption: Self-reported use at 750+ universities — unverified externally Free tier is 100 signup credits; paid from $99/yr. States GDPR compliance and has a privacy policy. Small SF startup; adoption claims are its own.

tools.name: Paper2Poster
tools.description: Multi-agent pipeline that converts a paper PDF into an editable PowerPoint conference poster: parses the paper into assets, plans a panel layout, renders and self-corrects with VLM feedback. Runs locally or via API models; Docker supported.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Fully automated paper-PDF-to-editable-pptx poster generation, open source and locally runnable Adoption: Accepted to NeurIPS 2025 Datasets & Benchmarks track; 3.9k GitHub stars; independent blog coverage (BrightCoding, Dec 2025) MIT license; needs an OpenAI API key or local vLLM models plus LibreOffice/poppler — technical setup, not point-and-click.

tools.name: Paper2Video
tools.description: Generates a complete conference presentation video from a paper: slides, synchronized subtitles, synthesized narration, cursor movements, and optional talking-head presenter from a reference photo and 10-second voice sample.
tools.notes:
[discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Automatic pre-recorded conference-talk video generation from a paper — relevant for virtual conferences requiring submitted videos Adoption: NeurIPS 2025 SEA workshop acceptance; 2.4k GitHub stars MIT license but demanding: LaTeX sources as input, Gemini/OpenAI keys, ~48GB-VRAM GPU for talking head (lighter slides-only mode exists). Research-grade, not turnkey.
[sweep 2026-09-11] vetted: alive (last commit 2026-03-05) but fails gate 2 (usable this week): needs LaTeX sources, two paid API keys and a 48GB GPU with no hosted demo; research artifact rather than a tool students can run. Keep candidate; revisit if a hosted service appears.

tools.name: PowerPoint Speaker Coach
tools.description: Rehearse a talk against your actual slide deck inside PowerPoint (web, Windows, Mac, mobile); flags pacing, pitch, filler words, monotone delivery, and reading text off slides, then produces a rehearsal report with statistics.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Delivery coaching bound to the actual conference deck, inside software every university already licenses — zero new accounts Adoption: Current Microsoft support documentation (fetched); UNC ITS 'Become a better public speaker' recommendation page seen in search results English-only interface requirement for the coach; needs microphone and internet. Free preview per Microsoft docs, but preview terms can change.

tools.name: VirtualSpeech
tools.description: Rehearse a talk in simulated rooms (conference room, lecture hall, press conference — 13 environments) via browser or VR headset; AI scores body language, eye contact, pace, and filler words, and asks questions generated from your presentation content.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Simulated-audience rehearsal in a virtual conference/lecture environment, including VR Adoption: G2 review page exists (seen in search); no academic library-guide adoption found $45/mo or $399/yr, no free trial found on pricing page; corporate-training oriented. UK company; EU-friendliness not confirmed.

tools.name: Yoodli
tools.description: Records a practice talk via webcam or uploaded video and scores filler words, pacing, eye contact, clarity, and structure, benchmarking each rehearsal against the last; AI follow-up questions simulate audience Q&A after a conference talk.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Quantified delivery feedback across repeated rehearsals of the same conference talk, plus simulated Q&A Adoption: Recommended on University of Hawai'i–West O'ahu official Distance Learning student-resources page (fetched); UW career-center resource page seen in search results Free tier is only 5 lifetime sessions; Pro $8/mo billed annually. Paid Advanced tier needed to exclude data from AI training.

tools.name: Audemic Scholar
tools.description: Reads uploaded or reference-manager-imported papers aloud with synchronized text highlighting; reorder sections, capture highlights and notes. Dyslexia-friendly fonts, background color options, and adjustable pacing support researchers with dyslexia, ADHD, or visual impairment.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Accessibility-adapted consumption of research papers (dyslexia, ADHD, visual impairment) Adoption: Site claims 40,000+ users from institutions; Berkeley SkyDeck-backed; iOS/Android app-store listings 7-day free trial then $20/mo or ~$109/yr. Listed awards/updates cluster in 2023; 2026 activity not directly confirmed.

tools.name: Cassyni
tools.description: Runs and records research seminars, then AI-enhances them: transcripts, slide extraction, semantic chapters, resolved references to cited papers, and a DOI per talk — turning seminars into citable, searchable scholarly objects researchers can browse.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: publishing and discovering research talks as DOI-citable parts of the scholarly record Adoption: Imperial College London Graduate School runs a Cassyni seminar program for PhD students; partnerships with Frontiers, Springer Nature, Elsevier, Royal Society (2023-2025 press) Attending/browsing seminars free; hosting a series is institutional/publisher-paid. Landing page is minimal; capabilities verified via press and Imperial pages.

tools.name: ElevenReader
tools.description: Free reader app from ElevenLabs that voices PDFs, preprints, and web articles with realistic neural voices, reading abbreviations naturally ('e.g.' as 'for example'). 10 free hours monthly; Ultra ($99/yr) adds smart imports that strip headers and footers.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Adoption: Genomics researcher Stephen Turner's 'Paired Ends' Substack (Apr 2025) documents using it to listen to preprints and papers General-purpose reader, not academia-specific; no citation skipping. GenFM podcast feature not confirmed on current site.

tools.name: Kudos
tools.description: Researcher creates a free showcase page explaining a publication in plain language; Kudos's AI service drafts the summary and a paid campaign promotes it via email, social media, and themed showcases, with tracked views, Altmetric scores, and citations.
tools.notes:
[discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Publishing and promoting plain-language summaries of published papers with impact tracking Adoption: Kudos blog documents AI Summaries rollout with publishers and author-verdict testing; university partnership coverage (Sheffield Hallam) seen in search results Free account is self-write; AI-drafted summary confirmed in the $499 researcher campaign and publisher services. Self-serve AI drafting on free tier unconfirmed.
[sweep 2026-09-11] provider normalised to legal name Kudos Innovations Ltd (site footer); otherwise unchanged.

tools.name: Listening
tools.description: Converts paper PDFs into natural-sounding audio that automatically skips citations, references, and footnotes; listen by section (abstract, results) at up to 4x speed. Mobile apps and Chrome extension for consuming a reading backlog while commuting.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Full-text listening to academic PDFs with citation/footnote skipping and section-level navigation Adoption: Site claims 50,000+ users; iOS/Android app-store presence; frequently compared in academic TTS roundups; no libguide sighting $12.99/mo or $39/yr promo; no free tier on pricing page (third-party listing mentions 1-week trial). GDPR posture unverified.

tools.name: PaperTok
tools.provider: University of Washington Prosocial Computing Group
tools.description: Generates roughly 45-second short-form explainer videos from an uploaded paper PDF using Gemini; the researcher iteratively edits the script and visuals before rendering, for TikTok/Reels-style science communication. Open-source codebase; presented at CHI 2026.
tools.notes:
[discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Paper to short-form social video for public science communication Adoption: CHI 2026 paper (Barcelona, April 2026); TechXplore coverage June 2026 Academic prototype, live site with generate button; requires user's paid Google Gemini subscription. Privacy policy and durability unverified.
[sweep 2026-09-11] Candidate vetted: passes gates 1, 3, 5; gate 2 marginal (needs user's paid Gemini subscription); FAILS gate 4 — no privacy policy on site, academic prototype with no durability commitment. Keep candidate; re-check if a privacy policy appears.

tools.name: Wondercraft
tools.description: Turns an uploaded paper or URL into a conversational podcast episode; edit the script word-by-word, choose or clone voices, add team review flows, then export WAV or publish toward Spotify and Apple Podcasts. Free tier includes starter credits.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Producing a publishable, edited outreach podcast episode from a paper (vs. NotebookLM's non-editable private overviews) General podcast studio with a dedicated research-paper workflow; free 150 credits, Creator $25/mo. Academic adoption unverified.

tools.name: CAS SciFinder Prior Art
tools.description: Inside CAS SciFinder: paste 200+ characters of invention text (claims or abstract) and AI algorithm streams return similar patents and non-patent literature published before your priority date, drawing on CAS's human-curated chemistry collection including Markush structures.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Chemistry-aware prior-art search over curated substance/Markush indexing — inside a database most chemistry-active universities already license, so no new procurement Adoption: Temple and Rutgers library AI-features guides both list Prior Art Discovery as an AI feature of CAS SciFinder Requires an institutional SciFinder subscription; direct product-help page returned 403, feature confirmed via cas.org and two libguides. CAS Newton conversational AI is a separate, newer layer.

tools.name: Google Patents
tools.description: Free worldwide patent full-text search with ML features: machine-classified CPC code suggestions, 'Similar' documents ranked by a full-text model, one-click 'Find prior art' scoped to before the priority date, SMILES chemical-structure search, and Google Scholar non-patent literature integration.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Zero-cost first-look prior-art check with priority-date-aware 'Find prior art' across patents, Scholar and Books simultaneously Adoption: Standard entry in university patent libguides (Michigan State, Iowa State, Texas A&M, Pitt appeared in searches); Google Research blog documents the Prior Art Finder Help page (support.google.com/faqs/answer/7049475) confirms features; main page is a JS app so feature claims verified via help page and libguides.

tools.name: InventGenie
tools.description: Turns research papers, notes and technical input into structured invention-disclosure building blocks: draft patent claims, specification text and figure suggestions, formatted for tech-transfer review, with multi-inventor collaboration. Pay-per-draft or monthly seat pricing (free trial); attorney review still required before filing.
tools.notes:
[discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: AI drafting of the invention disclosure itself, aimed explicitly at university researchers and tech transfer — the only researcher-facing (not attorney-facing) drafting tool found Real but young company; no independent academic adoption found; no free tier. Confidentiality caution: check TTO policy before pasting unfiled invention details into third-party AI (UC Berkeley OTL advises exactly this).
[sweep 2026-09-11] Vetted: passes all five gates (patents-tech-transfer stage; purchasable + free trial; researcher-facing disclosure drafting no general assistant structures; real company with privacy policy, terms, transparent pricing; alive). Recommend promote to active/extended. '$180' dropped from description — it is a 60%-off promotional price ($450 list). Keep the TTO-confidentiality caution.

tools.name: PatSnap
tools.description: AI innovation-intelligence platform: patent landscape maps, novelty and FTO search agents (Eureka), drafting agents, litigation and market data, biosequence and chemical structure search. Tech transfer offices use it to judge whether an invention's space is commercially active before funding proof-of-concept.
tools.notes: [discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: TTO-grade commercial landscape triage — 'who is active in this space and is it heating up' — before deciding to file Adoption: Published customer case study: City, University of London technology transfer office uses it for landscape analysis of academic inventions (replaced manual Espacenet work) Enterprise pricing via demo; Eureka offers a free trial. Recommendable mainly where the university already licenses it; individuals cannot simply subscribe at list price.

tools.name: PQAI
tools.provider: Project PQAI (nonprofit initiative, AT&T / Georgia IP Alliance)
tools.description: Paste a plain-language invention description; deep-learning models trained on examiner citation data return ranked prior art from USPTO, EPO and open-access journals, plus concept extraction and CPC/IPC code suggestions. Open-source (MIT); free web search, paid API tiers.
tools.notes:
[discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Free, open-source semantic prior-art search an academic can run before submitting an invention disclosure; API is explicitly pitched at university tech transfer offices Adoption: Unified Patents support article describes it; site has a 'For University Tech Transfer Offices' page; active GitHub org (pqaidevteam); 2025-2026 dated content Coverage is USPTO/EPO + DOAJ, not all jurisdictions; results are a first-pass screen, not a professional novelty search.
[sweep 2026-09-11] Site now lists API access as paid (tiered); web search still free. Description adjusted; MIT license not re-checked this sweep.

tools.name: The Lens
tools.provider: The Lens Limited (Australian non-profit, wholly owned subsidiary of SPIE; formerly Cambia)
tools.description: Links 155M+ patent records with 270M+ scholarly works: landscape dashboards, patent-to-paper citation mapping, PatSeq search for DNA/protein sequences inside patents, freedom-to-operate style filtering. Free personal accounts for academic researchers (exports up to 50,000 records); institutional toolkit for universities.
tools.notes:
[discovery 2026-08-18] Unique use case: Seeing which patents cite your own papers, and finding biological sequences buried in patents (PatSeq) — the scholarly-patent bridge no general assistant or single-corpus tool covers Adoption: Listed on WIPO Inspire; peer-reviewed review article in PMC; explicit cost-free academic personal accounts and Lens Equitable Access Program Ownership moved to non-profit The Lens Limited June 2026. Strength is authoritative linked data, not generative AI — release notes show few AI features; commercial individual use is $1,000/yr.
[sweep 2026-09-11] The Lens Limited is now a wholly owned subsidiary of SPIE (relaunch announced 2026-06-26); platform, free personal accounts and 50,000-record exports unchanged, so status stays active rather than acquired. $1,000/yr commercial figure not re-verified.

tools.name: Sage Policy Profiles
tools.description: Shows where your publications are cited in government policy documents via Overton's index; export, visualize, and share the matches. A matcher added 2026 surfaces up to three personalized policy-engagement opportunities monthly.
tools.notes: [grok-gap-hunt 2026-08-18, independently verified] Free + Overton confirmed on fetched sagepub.com press release (2023-12-07) and Feb 2026 blog; product homepage is JS-thin and names only Sage. 26,000+ users claimed.
